stem: Which word or phrase best shows how the second sentence relates to the first?
stimulus: Many people assume that the longest bridges are always the hardest ones to build, since every extra span adds more steel, more concrete, and more cost. ______ engineers often say that a short bridge over deep, fast-moving water can cause far greater problems than a long bridge over a calm, shallow bay.
explanation: Sentence one sets up a belief with 'many people assume': longer bridges are harder to build. Sentence two goes against that belief, because a short bridge can be the harder one. When a sentence undercuts what the one before it led you to expect, you need a concession word, and 'However' is the one offered here. This is the basic move behind every 'expectation, then surprise' transition question: spot the setup word ('assume', 'seem', 'long believed') and expect it to be overturned.

B.why: You saw that both sentences are about how hard bridges are to build and reached for an addition word. 'Moreover' says sentence two pushes the same point further, but sentence two pushes against it. Try 'and also' between the sentences: 'longer means harder, and also shorter can be harder' doesn't make sense.

C.why: You treated sentence two as following from sentence one. Nothing in the belief about long bridges causes engineers to say short bridges are harder. Their view comes from experience that contradicts the belief, not from the belief itself.

D.why: You read sentence two as one case of the general claim. A short, difficult bridge isn't an example of 'longest bridges are hardest'. It's a counterexample, so it disagrees with the claim instead of illustrating it.

stem: Which word or phrase best shows how the second sentence relates to the first?
stimulus: For much of the twentieth century, many economists believed that any increase in the minimum wage would lead employers to cut jobs, because paying each worker more would make it too costly to keep everyone. ______ a number of later studies comparing neighboring regions found little or no drop in employment after wages rose.
explanation: 'Many economists believed' marks sentence one as a belief that may be mistaken. Sentence two reports what the evidence showed, and it doesn't match the belief: jobs didn't fall. When sentence one is a mistaken belief and sentence two gives the real finding, 'Actually' is the natural correction word. This pattern turns up in transition questions whenever a passage opens with 'long believed' or 'many assumed'.

A.why: You noticed both sentences are about minimum wages and jobs and assumed one leads to the other. 'Therefore' would mean the belief caused the studies' result, but the result contradicts the belief. This is the trap of checking the topic but never checking the direction.

C.why: 'Similarly' says sentence two makes a matching point. The studies found the opposite of what economists expected, so the two sentences point in different directions.

D.why: 'For instance' would make the studies an example that supports the belief. They found no job losses, so they work against the belief rather than illustrating it.

stem: Which word or phrase best shows how the second sentence relates to the first?
stimulus: The Moon is the most closely studied object in the night sky. Astronomers have mapped nearly every crater on its near side, measured its distance to within centimeters, and brought back hundreds of kilograms of its rock. ______ a basic question remains unsettled: scientists still disagree about exactly how the Moon formed.
explanation: Sentence one lists big achievements, so you'd expect the Moon to be fully understood. Sentence two reports a gap: how it formed is still debated. A list of successes followed by something unresolved is expectation, then surprise, and 'Still' is the concession word that marks that turn. When a passage piles up accomplishments, check whether the next sentence pivots against them.

A.why: You picked a cause word because both sentences are about studying the Moon. All that study didn't cause the question to stay open. The open question survives despite the study, which is a concession, not a result.

B.why: You may have ruled out a contrast word because sentence one is all successes and nothing in it seemed to need disagreeing with. Sentence two isn't one more success, though. It points to what all that work hasn't settled, which is a turn against the list.

D.why: 'For instance' would make the formation debate one of the achievements listed in sentence one. It's the opposite: something astronomers haven't achieved.

stem: Which word or phrase best shows how the second sentence relates to the first?
stimulus: Gerardus Mercator's 1569 world map had several real strengths: sailors could plot a straight compass course across it, its coastlines were drawn with great care, and printers copied it for centuries. ______ the map badly distorts size near the poles, making Greenland look about as large as Africa, a continent roughly fourteen times its area.
explanation: Sentence one names a category, 'several real strengths', and lists them. Sentence two names a serious weakness. Those point in opposite directions: once you've granted the strengths, sentence two brings in a flaw that cuts against them. 'That said' is the concession word that does this ('all of that is true, but...'). This is the umbrella-then-turn pattern you'll meet in real transition questions.

A.why: You saw a list and assumed the next sentence adds one more item to it. 'Moreover' would make the distortion another strength. Try 'and also': '...printers copied it for centuries, and also it badly distorts size' sounds wrong, because it's a flaw, not a strength.

B.why: 'Namely' restates the thing just named more precisely. The thing named was 'several real strengths', and the distortion isn't one of them, so sentence two doesn't zoom in on sentence one at all.

D.why: You linked the two sentences because both describe the same map. The strengths don't cause the distortion. 'For this reason' claims a cause the passage never states, and the two sentences actually pull in opposite directions.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many people assume that a steel bridge keeps the same length all year, as solid and unchanging as the riverbanks it connects. ______ the steel in a long bridge can stretch by several centimeters on a hot summer afternoon. Engineers plan for this movement by leaving small gaps, called expansion joints, in the roadway.
explanation: Cover the choices and name what each sentence does. The first sentence states a belief: 'many people assume' the bridge never changes length. The second sentence says the opposite is true, because the steel stretches on hot days. When the first sentence is a mistaken belief and the second gives the real fact, you need a correction word, and 'Actually' says exactly that. This is the basic move behind every 'expectation, then surprise' transition question. If you can spot that sentence two goes against what sentence one leads you to expect, you can handle the longer versions on the real test.

B.why: You treated the second sentence as a result of the first. People's assumption does not make the steel stretch. The stretching goes against the assumption. Before you accept a cause word, check whether sentence one actually produces sentence two.

C.why: This is the subtype's trap. Both sentences are about the length of a steel bridge, so 'Moreover' felt like it fit, but you never checked the direction. 'Moreover' adds a point that agrees with the first sentence, and this sentence contradicts it. Try putting 'and also' between them. 'People assume it never changes, and also it stretches' sounds wrong.

D.why: 'For instance' introduces one example of what the first sentence just said. A bridge stretching is not an example of a bridge keeping the same length. It disproves that idea. An example has to agree with the claim it illustrates.
